entries.question: What is swimrun?
entries.answer: Swim, run, repeat. Teams (or soloists) move over a course that alternates between open-water swimming and trail running, in one go, with the same shoes and gear all the way.

entries.question: But can tigers actually swim?
entries.answer: Yes, and well. Tigers are among the few big cats that enjoy water: they cool off in it and swim across rivers. That is why a tiger is our swimrun mascot, and why the tiger in the logo is mid-swim.

entries.question: How many segments does a swimrun have?
entries.answer: It depends on the race. A short course may have a handful of swims and runs, a big island-hopping race has dozens. TigerLegs counts them for you: upload a GPX and it lists every swim and run segment.

entries.question: What are the distances in swimrun?
entries.answer: There are no standard distances. Every course is different: the swims can be a few hundred metres or several kilometres, and the runs anything from a short stretch of beach to long trails. That is exactly why measuring segments per course is useful.

entries.question: Do you swim in your running shoes?
entries.answer: Usually yes. Most swimrunners keep their shoes on and often use paddles and a pull buoy while swimming, plus a wetsuit that is easy to run in. More in our Substack series 'From zero till Ötillö': https://from0tillotillo.substack.com/

entries.question: What does TigerLegs stand for?
entries.answer: Terrain Informed Gpx ExtractoR: LEts Go Swimrun!

entries.question: Is my GPX file uploaded?
entries.answer: No. The analysis runs in your browser. Terrain data from OpenStreetMap is opt-in, and then only a coarse bounding box is sent, never your trackpoints. See the About page for details.
